title: This Bird Sees Two Summers a Year and Never a Winter
subject: Arctic tern

scenes.text: This bird lives through two summers a year and never sees winter.
The Arctic tern. Every year it flies from Greenland to Antarctica and back. About 44,000 miles.
Scientists strapped tiny 1.4-gram trackers to 60 of them to see how.
It doesn't fly straight. It takes an S-shaped route that rides the prevailing winds.
One bird logged 50,700 miles in a single year.
Over a lifetime, that adds up to three trips to the Moon and back. Two summers, no winter.

description:
The Arctic tern chases summer from the Arctic to Antarctica and back every year.
Tracking 60 birds with 1.4-gram geolocators showed an average round trip of about 44,000 miles, with the longest at 50,700 miles.
Would you fly pole to pole for endless summer?
first_comment: A tern's tracker weighed 1.4 grams. Which animal do you think has the longest migration on land?
